title.rendered: Declaring Over Your Mind: The Mind of Christ | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 8

excerpt.rendered: You already have the mind of Christ. Day 8 teaches believers how to declare peace, clarity, and renewed thinking in the Philippians 4:8 pattern.

content.rendered:
You will never think your way into peace. You must speak to the mind the Scriptures already gave you, the mind of Christ, until it begins to lead.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, October 25, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 8

Today’s Scripture

“For ‘who has known the mind of the Lord that he may instruct Him?’ But we have the mind of Christ.”
1 Corinthians 2:16 (NKJV)

“Finally, brethren, whatever things are true, whatever things are noble, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report, if there is any virtue and if there is anything praiseworthy, meditate on these things.”
Philippians 4:8 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Scripture is extraordinary. The NKJV states, flatly, in 1 Corinthians 2:16, “But we have the mind of Christ.” The AMPC expands it: “Now we have the mind of Christ (the Messiah) and do hold the thoughts (feelings and purposes) of His heart.” The TPT says, “We have the mind of Christ and hold his thoughts, feelings, and purposes.” This is not something God is going to grant us. It is already resident in every believer by the Spirit. Our problem is not acquisition; it is cooperation.

Anxiety, confusion, and racing thoughts are not evidence that God has forgotten you. They are often signals that another voice has been louder in your head than the Spirit of Christ. From Lagos, where a university student is overwhelmed by too many open tabs in his head, to London, where a professional battles 3 a.m. anxiety, to Manila, Nairobi and São Paulo, where mothers carry whole family burdens between the ears, Philippians 4:8 is a prescription. Meditate on what is true, noble, right, pure, lovely, admirable. Starve the mental voices that disagree with Scripture, and feed the ones that agree.

Jesus Himself refused to be ruled by His emotions. In Gethsemane He said, “Not My will, but Yours be done” (Luke 22:42), and ate the agony that followed by submitting His mind to His Father. On the cross, with pain pouring in from every nerve, He quoted Psalm 22 and Psalm 31, because when the storm hits, the mind of a redeemed child goes to Scripture, not to speculation. Declaration over the mind is simply speaking Scripture to your own thoughts until they settle under the Lordship of Christ.

Paul calls this “casting down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ” (2 Corinthians 10:5). You cannot evict a lie by thinking harder; you evict it by speaking truth over it, repeatedly, until your mind agrees. The mind of Christ is yours. The question is whether your words will summon it to the surface today.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. You already have the mind of Christ. Peace is not something you earn by overthinking; it is something you receive by renewing.

Personalise. Name the thoughts troubling you. Fear of the future. Shame from the past. A conversation that keeps replaying. Bring each one into the light.

Proclaim. Speak Philippians 4:8 and Isaiah 26:3 over your mind. “You will keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on You.” Keep speaking until the storm answers to the Prince of Peace.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I have the mind of Christ. I hold His thoughts, His feelings, and His purposes. My mind is renewed by the washing of the Word. I think on what is true, noble, right, pure, lovely, and praiseworthy. I cast down every argument and high thing that exalts itself above the knowledge of God. I bring every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ. Anxiety has no landing strip in my head. Confusion has no authority over me. The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guards my heart and my mind in Christ Jesus. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
